⚠ Browser XSD Limitation

Full XSD schema validation requires a server-side XML processor (like Java's JAXB, .NET's XmlSchema, or libxml2) because browsers do not expose a native XSD validation API. This tool performs structural XSD validation in the browser: it checks that every required element and attribute defined in the schema is present, data types are consistent, and no undefined elements appear. For strict production-grade XSD validation, use a server-side tool.

About XSD Validation

XSD (XML Schema Definition) defines the structure, data types, and constraints of an XML document. Well-formedness checks that XML is syntactically correct (properly nested tags, valid attributes, correct encoding). Schema validation additionally checks that the content matches the rules defined in the XSD — required elements, data types, value restrictions, and more.

What is a XSD Validator — XML Schema Validation?

An XSD (XML Schema Definition) validator checks that an XML document conforms to the rules defined in an XSD schema. It verifies required elements, data types, attribute constraints, and document structure beyond basic well-formedness.

Common Use Cases

Validating XML messages before sending to partner systems
Checking XML configuration files against their schema
Verifying SOAP request/response compliance
Validating XML data exports from enterprise systems
Testing XML document structure in development

Frequently Asked Questions

What is XSD?▼
XSD (XML Schema Definition) is a language for describing the structure and constraints of XML documents. It defines which elements and attributes are allowed, their data types, and whether they are required or optional.
What is the difference between well-formed and valid XML?▼
Well-formed XML follows basic XML syntax rules (proper nesting, closed tags). Valid XML is well-formed AND conforms to a specific schema (DTD or XSD).
Why does my valid XML fail schema validation?▼
Common causes: wrong namespace declarations, element name mismatches (XML is case-sensitive), missing required attributes, or data type violations.
